title: Posterior consistency at a KL projection

items.title: KL projection sets and relative KL neighborhoods
items.statement: For a jointly measurable dominated IID density model with truth P0 and metric parameter space (Theta,rho), define K(theta)=KL(P0||Ptheta), finite K*=inf K, the nonempty full minimizer set Theta*, distance d(theta,Theta*)=inf rho(theta,theta*), and relative neighborhoods B_epsilon={theta:K(theta)-K*<=epsilon}.
items.strategy: Definition: fix the KL direction, finite minimum, full projection set, metric distance, and relative-neighborhood convention.

items.title: A nonconstant centered integrable IID random walk is unbounded above
items.statement:
Let $(X_n)_{n\ge1}$ be IID real random variables with $\mathbb E|X_1|<\infty$, $\mathbb EX_1=0$, and $\mathbb P(X_1=0)<1$. Put $S_0=0$ and $S_n=\sum_{i=1}^nX_i$. Then
$$\mathbb P\left(\sup_{n\ge0}S_n=+\infty\right)=1.$$
In particular, $\limsup_{n\to\infty}S_n=+\infty$ almost surely.
items.axiom_use: None; the supplied real random variables use no selection.

references.title: Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition, §5.4, especially Theorem 5.4.8 (Chung–Fuchs recurrence)

items.title: Likelihood-tilted measures at a KL projection
items.statement: For selected theta* in Theta* with finite KL contrast and ptheta*>0 P0-a.s., define Qtheta(A)=integral_A (ptheta/ptheta*) dP0, with ratio zero where ptheta*=0, and qtheta=Qtheta(X) in [0,infinity]. A local lemma proves Qtheta sigma-finite; another proves Qtheta^n has product density relative to P0^n.
items.strategy: Definition: set the likelihood-ratio density and null-set convention; downstream local lemmas establish measure and product properties.

items.title: Likelihood tilts are sigma-finite measures
items.statement: Under the likelihood-tilt definition, Qtheta(A)=integral_A rtheta dP0 is a sigma-finite measure, since its density sublevel sets have finite Qtheta measure.
items.strategy: Direct: the nonnegative density defines a measure, and its integer sublevel sets give a countable finite-measure cover.

items.title: KL-neighborhood prior mass lower-bounds the likelihood denominator
items.statement: If B_epsilon is measurable with positive prior mass and its relative log likelihood contrasts are P0-integrable Pi-a.e., then for each alpha>epsilon the relative likelihood denominator D_n is eventually at least exp(-n alpha) P0-a.s.; it is finite and positive P0^n-a.s. for each n.
items.strategy: Direct: obtain a common almost-sure strong-law event by Tonelli, verify finite positive evidence under domination, and apply Fatou to rescaled likelihoods.

items.title: Product likelihood tilts have the product density
items.statement: For each theta and n>=1, Qtheta^n exists and has density product_i ptheta(x_i)/ptheta*(x_i) relative to P0^n.
items.strategy: Direct: define the product-density measure relative to P0^n, compare its rectangle values with Qtheta^n by Tonelli, and use uniqueness of sigma-finite product measure.

items.title: Compact models admit tests at a unique KL projection under fractional-moment continuity
items.statement:
Assume AC as required by the imported KL and likelihood-density conventions
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Let $(\Theta,\rho)$ be a compact metric space in its
metric topology ([[def-metric-compactness]], [[def-metric-space]]). Let
$p_\theta$ be jointly measurable finite-valued probability densities with
respect to one sigma-finite measure $\mu$, and let $P_0$ have supplied density
$p_0$. Suppose $\theta^*$ is the unique minimizer of
$\theta\mapsto\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_\theta)$ with finite minimum. For every
$\theta$, assume
$$\mathbb E_{P_0}\frac{p_\theta(X)}{p_{\theta^*}(X)}<\infty.$$
For every $\theta_1\ne\theta^*$, assume the extended relative contrast is
well-defined and satisfies
$$\mathbb E_{P_0}\log\frac{p_{\theta_1}(X)}{p_{\theta^*}(X)} =-\left[\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_{\theta_1})-\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_{\theta^*})\right]<0,$$
where the value $-\infty$ is allowed. For every such $\theta_1$, assume
that for all $s$ in some interval $(s_0,1)$ with $0\le s_0<1$, the finite
fractional-moment function
$$M_s(\theta_1,\theta):= \mathbb E_{P_0}\left[ \left(\frac{p_\theta(X)}{p_{\theta_1}(X)}\right)^s \cdot \left(\frac{p_\theta(X)}{p_{\theta^*}(X)}\right)^{1-s} \right]$$
is continuous at $\theta_1$. Define its integrand to be zero where
$p_\theta=0$, to be $+\infty$ where $p_\theta>0$ and $p_{\theta_1}=0$, and
to have the displayed value elsewhere; on the $P_0$-null set where
$p_{\theta^*}=0$, assign it value zero. Then, for every $\eta>0$, there are
measurable tests $\phi_n:\mathsf X^n\to[0,1]$ and constants
$c_\eta,C_\eta>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$,
$$P_0^n\phi_n\le C_\eta e^{-c_\eta n},\qquad \sup_{\theta:\rho(\theta,\theta^*)\ge\eta} Q_\theta^n(1-\phi_n)\le C_\eta e^{-c_\eta n}.$$
If the separated set is empty, take $\phi_n=0$. This sufficient
test construction is restricted to the stated compact, unique-minimizer
case; it asserts no generic testability on noncompact parameter spaces.
items.strategy: Direct: prove a fractional moment below one from a strictly negative extended log contrast, use continuity for local exponential tests, then cover the compact separated set finitely.

items.title: Exponential tests and KL mass force posterior exclusion
items.statement:
Let $V\subseteq\Theta$ be measurable. Suppose a relative KL neighborhood
$B_\epsilon$ has positive prior mass and that, for all sufficiently large
$n$, tests $\phi_n:\mathsf X^n\to[0,1]$ satisfy
$$\phi_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\longrightarrow0\quad P_0^\infty\text{-almost surely},\qquad \sup_{\theta\in V}Q_\theta^n(1-\phi_n)\le e^{-n\beta}$$
for a constant $\beta>\epsilon$. Then
$$\Pi(V\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)\longrightarrow0 \quad P_0^\infty\text{-almost surely}.$$
items.axiom_use: AC enters through the imported KL and likelihood-density conventions; supplied joint density representatives mean the proof makes no further selections.

references.title: B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises Theorem under Misspecification, Lemma 4.1, pp. 376–377

items.title: Posterior consistency at a KL projection
items.statement:
Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a sample space with a fixed sigma-finite
measure and let $(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ be a dominated experiment
([[def-dominated-statistical-experiment]]). Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T,\rho)$
be a metric parameter space with its Borel sigma-algebra
([[def-metric-space]]) and supplied
finite-valued likelihood densities $p_\theta$
([[def-likelihood-density]]) that are jointly measurable and normalized
relative to $\mu$. Let $P_0$ be a probability measure with supplied density
$p_0$ ([[def-probability-measure]]) and let
$X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be IID with law $P_0$
([[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]). Let $\Pi$ be a
prior probability on $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ ([[def-probability-measure]]).
Assume AC for the imported directional KL and likelihood-density
conventions. Define
$K(\theta)$, $K^*$, and the nonempty set $\Theta^*$ as in
[[def-kl-projection-set-and-relative-kl-neighborhoods]]. Assume $K^*<\infty$
and, for every $\epsilon>0$, the measurable set
$$\Pi\{\theta:K(\theta)-K^*\le\epsilon\}>0.$$
Fix any selected $\theta^*\in\Theta^*$ and assume that for
$\Pi$-almost every $\theta$ in each such set,
$\log(p_\theta/p_{\theta^*})$ is $P_0$-integrable, as required by the
denominator lemma. Define the likelihood-tilted measures $Q_\theta$ as in
[[def-likelihood-tilted-measure-at-kl-projection]]. Define the posterior by
[[thm-bayes-formula-for-dominated-kernels]] on finite positive evidence
fibres; the denominator lemma below makes those fibres $P_0^n$-almost sure.
For each $n\ge1$, use the product measure $Q_\theta^n$ and its $P_0^n$
density from [[lem-product-likelihood-tilt-has-product-density]].
Assume the test integrals below are well-defined. For every $\eta>0$,
suppose there are
measurable tests $\phi_n:\mathsf X^n\to[0,1]$ and a constant $\beta_\eta>0$ such that
$$\phi_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\longrightarrow0\quad P_0^\infty\text{-almost surely},\qquad \sup_{\theta:\,d(\theta,\Theta^*)>\eta} Q_\theta^n(1-\phi_n)\le e^{-n\beta_\eta}$$
for all sufficiently large $n$,
where $d(\theta,\Theta^*)=\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta^*}\rho(\theta,\vartheta)$.
Then
$$\Pi\{\theta:d(\theta,\Theta^*)>\eta\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n\} \longrightarrow0 \quad P_0^\infty\text{-almost surely}$$
for every fixed $\eta>0$. The type-I expectations need not be summable or exponentially small.
items.axiom_use: AC enters through the imported KL and likelihood-density conventions. The jointly measurable density family is supplied, so the proof makes no further selections.

references.title: B. J. K. Kleijn and A. W. van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises Theorem under Misspecification, §4.1, Lemma 4.1 and Corollary 4.2, pp. 376–379
B. J. K. Kleijn, Bayesian Statistics for Frequentists, §5.3.1, pp. 158–160
R. V. Ramamoorthi, K. Sriram, and R. Martin, On Posterior Concentration in Misspecified Models, §§1–3

title: Posterior consistency at a KL projection — Examples

items.title: Distant alternatives can prevent uniform testability
items.statement: For truth (1/2,1/2) and alternatives p_j=(1/2-delta_j,1/2+delta_j) with delta_j=1/(j+4), the unique minimizer is the truth at label 0, but parameter-distant alternatives preclude tests with both vanishing type-I and uniformly vanishing type-II errors.
items.strategy: Verification: construct a finite-coordinate coupling with disagreement at most n delta_j, then derive the testing-error lower bound from total variation.

items.title: A nonunique KL projection set need not select one parameter
items.statement: When two labels share density (1/2,1/2), both minimize KL for truth (3/5,2/5); a third density (1/5,4/5) has larger KL loss, its posterior mass vanishes, and the two minimizer labels retain their prior odds.
items.strategy: Verification: compute the third-point KL loss, use equal minimizer likelihoods, and apply the IID strong law to the log odds against the third point.

items.title: A finite misspecified model with a unique KL projection
items.statement: For explicit two-point densities p0=(3/5,2/5), pa=(1/2,1/2), pb=(1/5,4/5), the unique KL minimizer is a, the posterior mass at b tends to zero almost surely, and Qb(X)=22/25.
items.strategy: Verification: compute the exact KL contrast and tilt mass; apply the IID strong law to bounded log posterior odds.

items.title: A likelihood tilt can be a finite measure of mass below one
items.statement: For p0=(1/10,9/10), pa=(9/10,1/10), and pb=(1,0), a is the unique KL minimizer and Qb(X)=1/9.
items.strategy: Verification: compare the finite and infinite directional KL losses, then evaluate the likelihood-ratio integral on the two-point space.

items.title: A likelihood tilt can be a finite measure of mass above one
items.statement: For p0=(1/1000,999/1000), pa=(10^-6,999999/10^6), and pb=(1,0), a is the unique KL minimizer and Qb(X)=1000.
items.strategy: Verification: compare finite and infinite directional KL losses, then evaluate the likelihood-ratio integral exactly.

items.title: Weak tests against likelihood tilts do not ensure almost-sure posterior consistency
items.statement:
In a dominated IID model with a finite KL minimum, a nonempty KL-minimizer
set $\Theta^*$, and positive prior mass in every relative KL neighborhood,
suppose that for every $\eta>0$ there are measurable tests satisfying
$$P_0^n\phi_n\to0,\qquad\sup_{\theta:d(\theta,\Theta^*)>\eta}Q_\theta^n(1-\phi_n)\to0.$$
The false assertion is that these conditions, allowing arbitrary
sigma-finite likelihood tilts, imply almost-sure posterior concentration
on every neighborhood of $\Theta^*$. The example below has a unique
minimizer and finite log likelihood contrasts, but posterior mass outside
each discrete neighborhood of radius less than one has almost-sure
limes superior one.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited only through the KL and likelihood-density conventions. Every density is supplied explicitly and each deterministic hitting-time quantile is chosen as the least admissible integer.

references.title: Kleijn and van der Vaart, The Bernstein-Von-Mises theorem under misspecification, Lemma 3.3 and Corollaries 4.1–4.2 (claims examined here)
Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition, random walks and zero-one laws
